## Explanation of the task 2

Task 2 examined whether participants could combine information about estimated voltage
and its uncertainty to locate a relevant spatial region. On each trial, participants saw
one EEG topoplot and were asked to select the scalp region with the highest
signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), defined as the absolute average-referenced voltage divided
by its standard error. They responded using a separate scalp layout divided into 64
selectable regions.

The task included three characteristic ERP patterns: MMN, P3, and N170. Each was shown
using each of the seven visualization types. This produced 21 trials per participant,
each on a separate page. Trial order was randomized separately for every participant.

![Example uncertainty-integration trial. Participants selected one of 64 regions after
identifying the region with the highest SNR.](<../The Art of Uncertain Topoplots/figures/task2_explainer_64_regions.png>){#fig-task2-explainer width=100% fig-alt="An example signal-to-noise-ratio topoplot beside a scalp selection grid divided into 64 regions. A pointer illustrates selecting one region on the grid."}

```{r shared-setup}
#| include: false
source("scripts/analysis_setup.R")
```

## Response scoring and trial reconstruction

- For each participan we reconstructed presentation order. Each participant went through 21 randomly shuffled pages.

- For each trial, survey recorded the visualization, ERP stimulus shown
  and one region selected by participant. There were 64 regions on selectable grid.

- The selected region was matched to the corresponding stimulus and its stored region score in `regions.txt`.

- The region score represents |Voltage|/SE at that region. This calcaulation is actually more complicated. 

::: {.callout-note title="How the 0–1 region score was calculated" collapse="true"}

For each stimulus, the scoring pipeline performed the following steps:

1. It loaded one average-referenced ERP case using the task, subject, time point, and
   condition recorded in `task_configs_30_balanced`. The fixed combinations were:

   | ERP pattern | Time point (index) | Condition |
   |:------------|-------------------:|----------:|
   | MMN         |                 96 |         3 |
   | N170        |                105 |         2 |
   | P3          |                129 |         1 |

2. It average-referenced the voltage across the $N$ channels:

   $$
   V_i^{AR} = V_i - \frac{1}{N}\sum_j V_j.
   $$

3. It calculated a polarity-independent, t-like signal-to-noise value at each channel:

   $$
   T_i = \frac{|V_i^{AR}|}{SE_i}.
   $$

4. It interpolated the channel-level $T_i$ values into a continuous topoplot grid. Only
   finite interpolated cells inside the visible head mask were retained.

5. It fitted the saved 64-region polygon template to the topoplot domain. For each
   region $k$, it averaged all retained grid cells that were inside both the polygon and
   the head mask:

   $$
   R_k = \operatorname{mean}\{T(x,y):(x,y)\in\text{region}_k\}.
   $$

6. It min--max normalized the 64 raw region scores separately within each stimulus:

   $$
   S_k = \frac{R_k - \min_j R_j}{\max_j R_j - \min_j R_j}.
   $$

   The weakest region therefore receives 0, the strongest receives 1, and other regions
   are positioned proportionally between them. Scores are rounded to two decimal places.

**Implementation references.** The stimulus-generation source is stored under
`UnfoldMakie/experiments/working/`:

- stimulus selection: `stimuli_data.jl:213`;
- average referencing and channel score: `region_detection/rereferencing.jl:96`;
- topoplot interpolation: `region_detection/region_score_exports.jl:48`;
- polygon validation and fitting: `get_regions.jl:19`;
- regional averaging: `region_detection/scoring.jl:338`;
- normalization, rounding, and export: `region_detection/region_score_exports.jl:7`.

The polygon definitions are stored in
`experiments/figures/task2_topo_regions_64_eeg_aligned_pipeline28/regions.jl`.

```{r}
task2_order <- data %>%
  select(ID, A207_01:A207_21) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -ID,
    names_to = "trial",
    names_prefix = "A207_",
    values_to = "position"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ID = as.character(ID),
    trial = as.integer(trial),
    position = as.integer(position)
  )
```

```{r}
task2_design <- data %>%
  select(ID, A205_01) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(A205_01, sep = "###") %>%
  filter(A205_01 != "") %>%
  transmute(
    ID,
    trial   = as.integer(get_field(A205_01, "trial")),
    vistype = get_field(A205_01, "vistype"),
    pattern = get_field(A205_01, "pattern"),
    subject = as.integer(get_field(A205_01, "subject")),
    stimulus = get_field(A205_01, "stim"),
    img_url  = get_field(A205_01, "imgUrl"),
    input_id = get_field(A205_01, "inputId")
  )

task2_responses <- data %>%
  select(ID, A201_01:A201_21) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -ID,
    names_to = "input_id",
    values_to = "selected_region"
  )
```

```{r}
score_text <- paste(
  readLines(project_path("regions.txt"), encoding = "UTF-8"),
  collapse = "\n"
)
score_matches <- stringr::str_match_all(
  score_text,
  '"([^"]+)"\\s*=>\\s*array\\(([^)]*)\\)'
)[[1]]
region_scores <- tibble::tibble(
  stimulus = score_matches[, 2],
  values = score_matches[, 3]
) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(values, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
  group_by(stimulus) %>%
  mutate(
    region = sprintf("R%02d", row_number()),
    score = as.numeric(values)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(stimulus, region, score)
```

```{r}
task2 <- task2_design %>%
  mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>%
  left_join(task2_responses %>% mutate(ID = as.character(ID)),
            by = c("ID", "input_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    region_number = readr::parse_number(selected_region),
    region = sprintf("R%02d", region_number)
  ) %>%
  left_join(region_scores, by = c("stimulus", "region")) %>%
  left_join(task2_order, by = c("ID", "trial")) %>%
  select(ID, trial, position, vistype, pattern, stimulus, region, score)
```

## Descriptive detection scores

- The analysis contains 2,394 responses: 114 participants x 21 trials. Each visualization
  type therefore has 342 responses: 114 participants x 3 ERP patterns.

 - No reconstructed responses were excluded for missing model variables. All 2,394 records
  contained participant, stimulus, visualization type, pattern, position, and score.

- Visualization type was treated as a categorical variable, with Basic topoplot as the
  reference condition. ERP pattern and stimulus were retained for the extended model.

- Presentation position was represented by `position_c = position - 11`. Thus,
  `position_c = 0` represents position 11, negative values represent earlier trials, and
  positive values represent later trials.

```{r}
task2_model <- task2 %>%
  transmute(
    ID = factor(ID),
    stimulus = factor(stimulus),
    vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
    pattern = factor(pattern),
    position_c = as.integer(position) - 11,
    score = as.numeric(score)
  ) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

stimulus_pattern_counts <- task2_model |>
  distinct(stimulus, pattern) |>
  count(stimulus)

stopifnot(
  nrow(task2_model) == nrow(task2),
  all(stimulus_pattern_counts$n == 1)
)
```

```{r task2-score-distribution}
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Distribution of the 2,394 trial-level detection scores. Bars show frequencies at
#|   the recorded two-decimal score resolution. A score of 0 indicates selection of the
#|   weakest region for a stimulus, whereas 1 indicates selection of the strongest region.
#|   Intermediate values preserve graded performance.

task2_score_distribution <- task2_model |>
  transmute(score_index = as.integer(round(score * 100))) |>
  count(score_index, name = "responses") |>
  tidyr::complete(
    score_index = 0:100,
    fill = list(responses = 0L)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    score = score_index / 100,
    score_type = if_else(
      score_index %in% c(0L, 100L),
      "Boundary score",
      "Intermediate score"
    ),
    percentage = 100 * responses / sum(responses),
    label_hjust = if_else(score_index == 0L, 0, 1)
  )

stopifnot(
  sum(task2_score_distribution$responses) == nrow(task2_model),
  all(task2_score_distribution$score >= 0),
  all(task2_score_distribution$score <= 1)
)

task2_score_distribution_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_score_distribution,
  aes(x = score, y = responses, fill = score_type)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.009) +
  geom_text(
    data = task2_score_distribution |>
      filter(score_index %in% c(0L, 100L)),
    aes(
      label = sprintf("n = %d (%.1f%%)", responses, percentage),
      hjust = label_hjust
    ),
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = 5,
    colour = "#111111",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Intermediate score" = "#6BAED6",
      "Boundary score" = "#08519C"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    "Detection score (0 = weakest region, 1 = strongest region)",
    limits = c(-0.01, 1.01),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    "Number of responses",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of detection scores") +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 22),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 20)
  )

task2_score_distribution_figure

ggsave(
  project_path("figures", "task2_score_distribution_figure.png"),
  task2_score_distribution_figure,
  width = 9,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 180,
  device = ragg::agg_png,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r task2-descriptive-gradient-plot}
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Detection scores summarized from participant-level means, with gradient uncertainty.
#|   For each visualization, the black line and number show the mean across participants;
#|   the dark-blue region shows the 95% confidence interval around that mean.

task2_gradient_order <- task2_table |>
  arrange(median) |>
  pull(vistype) |>
  as.character()

task2_gradient_participants <- task2_model |>
  group_by(ID, vistype) |>
  summarise(
    participant_score = mean(score),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

task2_gradient_summary <- task2_gradient_participants |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    n_participants = n(),
    mean_score = mean(participant_score),
    se_score = sd(participant_score) / sqrt(n_participants),
    df = n_participants - 1,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = task2_gradient_order),
    y_position = as.numeric(vistype),
    lower_95 = mean_score - qt(0.975, df) * se_score,
    upper_95 = mean_score + qt(0.975, df) * se_score
  ) |>
  arrange(vistype)

task2_gradient_means <- setNames(
  task2_gradient_summary$mean_score,
  as.character(task2_gradient_summary$vistype)
)
task2_gradient_value <- function(vistype) {
  sprintf("%.2f", task2_gradient_means[[vistype]])
}
task2_gradient_difference <-
  task2_gradient_means[["triple_CI"]] -
  task2_gradient_means[["bivariate_corner"]]

stopifnot(
  all(
    task2_gradient_summary$n_participants ==
      n_distinct(task2_model$ID)
  )
)

task2_gradient_data <- task2_gradient_summary |>
  tidyr::crossing(score = seq(0.5, 0.8, length.out = 241)) |>
  mutate(
    t_distance = abs(score - mean_score) / se_score,
    confidence_level = 2 * pt(t_distance, df) - 1,
    gradient_alpha = if_else(
      confidence_level <= 0.95,
      1,
      pmax(0, (1 - confidence_level) / 0.05)
    )
  )

task2_gradient_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_gradient_data,
  aes(x = score, y = y_position)
) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(alpha = gradient_alpha),
    width = 1 / 800,
    height = 0.62,
    fill = "#6BAED6"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = task2_gradient_summary,
    aes(
      x = mean_score,
      xend = mean_score,
      y = y_position - 0.31,
      yend = y_position + 0.31
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.8,
    colour = "#111111"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = task2_gradient_summary,
    aes(
      x = mean_score,
      y = y_position + 0.42,
      label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_score)
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 6
  ) +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    "Participant-level mean score",
    limits = c(0.5, 0.8),
    breaks = seq(0.5, 0.8, 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = task2_gradient_summary$y_position,
    labels = unname(
      vistype_labels[as.character(task2_gradient_summary$vistype)]
    ),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 0.65))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Detection task accuracy",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 22),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.text.y = element_text(lineheight = 0.75),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y = element_blank()
  )
```

## Detection-score analysis

- The primary analysis uses the extended model:

  ```r
  score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus)
  ```

- The outcome contains exact 0 and 1 values as well as intermediate scores. An
  ordered-beta model retains this graded information while supporting the complete closed
  interval from 0 to 1. A binary logistic model would instead treat every score below 1
  as equally incorrect.

- Every participant completed 21 trials, so responses from the same participant are
  related. Adding `(1 | ID)` gives each participant their own baseline detection
  performance while estimating common visualization, pattern, and presentation-position
  effects.

- Some stimuli may be intrinsically easier to interpret than others. Adding
  `(1 | stimulus)` gives each stimulus its own baseline score, so visualization
  comparisons are not attributed to stimulus difficulty alone.

- ERP pattern and centered presentation position adjust the visualization comparisons for
  the displayed pattern and for linear change as participants progressed through the task.

- The simpler base model is shown first as a reference. It contains visualization type
  and a participant random intercept but does not adjust for pattern, presentation
  position, or differences among stimuli.

```{r}
model_task2_base <- glmmTMB(
  score ~ vistype + (1 | ID),
  family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_model
)

summary(model_task2_base)$coefficients$cond |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  transmute(
    term = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      `(Intercept)` = "Basic topoplot (intercept)",
      vistypeadjacent = "Adjacent plots vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeanimation = "Animation vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_corner = "Bivariate corner vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_range = "Bivariate range vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypetriple_CI = "Confidence intervals vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeuncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers vs Basic topoplot",
      .default = term
    ),
    estimate = Estimate,
    standard_error = .data[["Std. Error"]],
    z_value = .data[["z value"]],
    p_value = format_pvalue_html(.data[["Pr(>|z|)"]])
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Term",
      "Estimate (logit scale)",
      "Standard error",
      "z value",
      "p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Fixed effects for the base sensitivity detection-score model.",
      "Values with p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Ordered-beta mixed model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>score ~ vistype + (1 | ID)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Coefficient scale:</strong> Logit scale.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Why correlated participant-specific visualization slopes were not retained" collapse="true"}
We tested whether the effect of visualization type differed between participants by
adding correlated participant-specific visualization effects: `(1 + vistype | ID)`.
The model could not estimate this full structure reliably:

- It ended with convergence code 1, a non-positive-definite Hessian, and singular
  convergence.

- The structure requires seven participant-level random coefficients and 28
  variance--covariance parameters.

- Each participant provided only three detection scores for each visualization type,
  which did not contain enough information to estimate all those parameters reliably.

We also tested simpler participant-specific structures:

- A participant-specific position slope converged, but its estimated standard deviation
  was only 0.006.

- A diagonal visualization structure, `diag(0 + vistype | ID)`, converged with a
  positive-definite Hessian. It estimates separate participant-specific visualization
  variances without estimating their correlations.

We therefore retained participant and stimulus random intercepts in the primary model.
This does not show that visualization effects are identical for every participant. It
means that these data cannot reliably estimate the full correlated structure. The
diagonal model remains available as a sensitivity analysis.
:::

```{r}
model_task2_no_vistype <- update(
  model_task2,
  . ~ . - vistype
)

anova(model_task2_no_vistype, model_task2) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("model") |>
  mutate(
    model = dplyr::recode(
      model,
      model_task2_no_vistype = "Covariates without visualization type",
      model_task2 = "Covariates with visualization type",
      .default = model
    ),
    `Pr(>Chisq)` = format_pvalue_html(.data[["Pr(>Chisq)"]])
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Model",
      "Parameters",
      "AIC",
      "BIC",
      "Log likelihood",
      "Deviance",
      "Likelihood-ratio chi-square",
      "df difference",
      "p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Likelihood-ratio test of visualization type for detection score.",
      "Values with p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model family:</strong> Ordered-beta mixed models with a logit ",
    "link.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Full model:</strong> ",
    "<code>score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + ",
    "(1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reduced model:</strong> The same model without ",
    "<code>vistype</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Comparison:</strong> The likelihood-ratio test evaluates whether ",
    "adding visualization type improves model fit.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model comparison"
)
```

**Figure method.** The points are estimated marginal mean detection scores from
the extended ordered-beta mixed model
`score ~ visualization type + pattern + centered position + (1 | participant) + (1 | stimulus)`,
fitted with a logit link. Estimates are evaluated at the middle presentation
position (`position_c = 0`, corresponding to position 11), averaged equally
over the MMN, N170, and P3 patterns, and calculated with participant and
stimulus random intercepts set to zero. They are then back-transformed to the
0–1 detection-score scale. Error bars are asymptotic pointwise 95% confidence
intervals for these model-estimated scores.

```{r}

detection_axis_colours <- ifelse(
  levels(task2_estimates$vistype) == "basic",
  "#377EB8",
  "#222222"
)

detection_score_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_estimates,
  aes(
    x = predicted_score,
    y = vistype,
    colour = vistype == "basic"
  )
) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      xmin = lower_ci,
      xmax = upper_ci
    ),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.14,
    linewidth = 0.55
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::percent(predicted_score, accuracy = 1)),

    },
    expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "#377EB8"),

  ) +
```

### Detection-score differences relative to Basic topoplot

**Figure method.** The contrasts use the same extended model and reference grid
as the estimated-score figure. Estimated marginal means are first
back-transformed to the response scale, and each visualization is then compared
with Basic topoplot. The six confidence intervals use the `emmeans` Dunnett-x
adjustment for multiple comparisons against a common reference. An interval
crossing zero indicates that the corresponding visualization is not clearly
different from Basic at the familywise 95% confidence level.

```{r task2-basic-contrast-figure}
task2_basic_reference <- which(
  emm_task2_response@levels$vistype == "basic"
)

task2_basic_contrasts_raw <- contrast(
  emm_task2_response,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = task2_basic_reference
) |>
  confint() |>
  as.data.frame()

task2_lower_ci_column <- grep(
  "lower.CL$|asymp.LCL$",
  names(task2_basic_contrasts_raw),
  value = TRUE
)[1]
task2_upper_ci_column <- grep(
  "upper.CL$|asymp.UCL$",
  names(task2_basic_contrasts_raw),
  value = TRUE
)[1]

task2_basic_contrasts <- task2_basic_contrasts_raw |>
  transmute(
    vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
    difference = estimate,
    lower_ci = .data[[task2_lower_ci_column]],
    upper_ci = .data[[task2_upper_ci_column]]
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = levels(task2_estimates$vistype))
  )

task2_contrast_limit <- max(
  abs(c(task2_basic_contrasts$lower_ci, task2_basic_contrasts$upper_ci)),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
task2_contrast_limit <- max(
  0.05,
  ceiling(task2_contrast_limit / 0.05) * 0.05
)

task2_contrast_labels <- c(
  adjacent = "Adjacent plots",
  bivariate_corner = "Bivariate corners",
  bivariate_range = "Bivariate range",
  triple_CI = "Confidence intervals",
  uncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers",
  animation = "Animation"
)

detection_score_contrast_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_basic_contrasts,
  aes(x = difference, y = vistype)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    colour = "#377EB8"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.14,
    linewidth = 0.55,
    colour = "#333333"
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#333333") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = ifelse(
      abs(difference) < 0.005,
      "0 pp",
      sprintf("%+.0f pp", 100 * difference)
    )),
    nudge_y = 0.32,
    vjust = 0.5,
    size = 5.5,
    colour = "#333333"
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = function(x) unname(task2_contrast_labels[x]),
    expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(-task2_contrast_limit, task2_contrast_limit),
    labels = function(x) ifelse(
      abs(x) < 0.005,
      "0 pp",
      sprintf("%+.0f pp", 100 * x)
    ),
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.04)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Detection task score differences",
    subtitle = "Response-scale contrasts with 95% confidence intervals",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 22),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 24, margin = margin(r = 12)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y = element_blank()
  )

detection_score_contrast_caption <- ggplot() +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.497,
    y = 0.5,
    label = "Difference in estimated detection score vs",
    hjust = 1,
    size = 20 / ggplot2::.pt,
    family = "Lato",
    colour = "#222222"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.503,
    y = 0.5,
    label = "Basic topoplot",
    hjust = 0,
    size = 20 / ggplot2::.pt,
    family = "Lato",
    colour = "#377EB8"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +
  theme_void()

detection_score_contrast_figure <-
  detection_score_contrast_figure /
  detection_score_contrast_caption +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.10))

detection_score_contrast_figure
```

## Completion-time analysis

- Completion time was reconstructed from the 21 page-timing variables and linked to each
  trial by participant and presentation position.

- Only non-missing positive times with an identified visualization type were retained. The
  descriptive table removes extreme times separately within each visualization type using
  the project's IQR rule; the mixed model retains all positive times.

- The model analyzes log completion time because trial times are positive and typically
  right-skewed:

  ```r
  log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID)
  ```

- The participant random intercept allows participants to have different typical response
  speeds. Presentation position adjusts for linear changes in speed across the 21 trials.
  Model estimates and confidence intervals are converted back from log time to seconds.

```{r task2-time-data}
task2_time <- data %>%
  select(ID, TIME029:TIME049) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -ID,
    names_to = "time_var",
    values_to = "time_sec"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ID = as.character(ID),
    # TIME029:TIME049 correspond to experimental positions 1:21.
    position = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(time_var, "TIME")) - 28L,
    time_sec = readr::parse_double(as.character(time_sec))
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    task2 %>%
      transmute(
        ID = as.character(ID),
        position,
        trial,
        vistype
      ),
    by = c("ID", "position")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(time_sec), !is.na(vistype), time_sec > 0)
```

### Model-estimated completion time

```{r task2-time-model}
task2_time_model <- task2_time %>%
  transmute(
    ID = factor(ID),
    vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
    position = as.integer(position),
    time_sec = as.numeric(time_sec)
  ) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.), time_sec > 0) %>%
  mutate(position_c = position - mean(position))

task2_time_fit <- lmer(
  log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID),
  data = task2_time_model
)

task2_time_estimates <- emmeans(
  task2_time_fit,
  ~ vistype,
  type = "response"
) %>%
  confint() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(
    vistype,
    estimated_time = response,
    lower_ci = lower.CL,
    upper_ci = upper.CL
  ) %>%
  arrange(estimated_time) %>%
  mutate(vistype = factor(vistype, levels = vistype))

task2_time_estimates |>
  mutate(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    across(
      c(estimated_time, lower_ci, upper_ci),
      \(x) round(x, 1)
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Estimated time (seconds)",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Model-estimated detection-task completion time",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Gaussian linear mixed model for log completion ",
    "time: <code>log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Presentation position:</strong> Estimates were calculated at the ",
    "average presentation position.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Output scale:</strong> Estimates and 95% confidence intervals were ",
    "back-transformed from log time to seconds.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```
